design.design:
PRINCIPLE
- One authoritative record, med_orders, plus a ledger, med_order_events. The four existing tables stay, each demoted to one role: medications = the WARD PROJECTION (about 20 readers keep working); helix_patient_med_orders = the SUPPLY child (one row per dispense request, many per order); orders (medication) = the CPOE VIEW of a draft; medication_administrations = the MAR child. Nothing is renamed, rebuilt or dropped.
- Strangler with two written invariants:
  I1. The dose decision never depends on the store being in sync for a fact the projection already carries. The verification fact lives on medications.verified_by/verified_at, which EVERY verify path writes (legacy and store). The store adds only what the projection cannot express: held (and, after MO-R1, verify-before-dose). A legacy writer that updates a linked row can therefore never make a verified drug ungivable.
  I2. Every code path that mutates a LINKED row writes through medorder_service, keyed on the link and not the flag: legacy verify and reject, /orders transitions on linked CPOE orders, Helix transitions and receipt on linked supply rows, and the eMAR. Unlinked rows keep exactly today's semantics.
- Flag promise, stated precisely: with both flags off on a database that never ran lifecycle mode, every check, screen, query and response behaves as at cafe363; the only difference on a database that ran record mode is that link-keyed mirrors keep appending store rows. A database that ran lifecycle mode keeps held orders ungivable and linked CPOE orders managed by the store after the flag goes off (fails closed, MO-R9).

1. DATA MODEL
One additive migration, numbered with the next free number after 47 at merge time (never pre-assigned; five sibling epics and about ten sessions share migrations.py). No declared FOREIGN KEYs on new tables (m20 rule 1), so they are never FK parents and a later CHECK widening is an ordinary in-transaction rebuild.

med_orders:
- id TEXT PRIMARY KEY (uuid4); patient_id TEXT NOT NULL; admission_id TEXT
- encounter_type TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'ip' CHECK in ('ip','op','discharge') (reserved for OPD)
- status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK in ('draft','prescribed','verified','held','stopped','completed','cancelled','rejected')
- held_from TEXT (the state a resume returns to); version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1
- source TEXT NOT NULL: chart | cpoe | order_set | sage_handoff | relay_agentic | helix_approve | scribe_extracted | history_import | legacy_adopted | verbal
- needs_verification INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 (1 for today's _UNVERIFIED_SOURCES)
- drug_name TEXT NOT NULL; formulary_id TEXT (exact helix_medication_master.id, never LIKE)
- dose, route, frequency TEXT; schedule_kind TEXT (nurse_shift_service.parse_frequency kind)
- is_prn INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0; prn_indication TEXT
- priority TEXT CHECK in ('routine','urgent','stat'); start_at, end_at, duration_text, indication, notes TEXT
- supply_source TEXT CHECK in ('pharmacy','ward_stock','patient_own') NULL (NULL until MO-R12)
- entered_by TEXT NOT NULL, entered_by_role TEXT; prescriber_id, prescribed_at; verified_by, verified_at
- status_reason, status_changed_by, status_changed_at
- last_safety_json, last_screened_at, screen_fingerprint
- projection_status TEXT CHECK in ('active','prn') NULL (NULL whenever the order is not live)
- legacy_medication_id INTEGER; cpoe_order_id TEXT; order_set_application_id INTEGER; sage_action_id, sage_handoff_id, scribe_note_id TEXT
- idempotency_key TEXT; facility_id TEXT (NULL = single site)
- created_at, updated_at TEXT via services.clinical_time.utc_iso_now()
Indexes: (patient_id, status); (status, needs_verification); (cpoe_order_id); (admission_id); UNIQUE(legacy_medication_id) WHERE NOT NULL; UNIQUE(idempotency_key) WHERE NOT NULL.

med_order_events (append-only by design):
- id INTEGER PK AUTOINCREMENT; med_order_id TEXT NOT NULL; patient_id TEXT NOT NULL
- kind: created | signed | verified | rejected | held | resumed | stopped | completed | cancelled | amended | adopted | supply_requested | supply_reviewing | supply_verified | dispensed | received | administered | not_given
- from_status, to_status, actor_id, actor_role, entry_point, reason, ref_type, ref_id, payload_json, idempotency_key (UNIQUE partial), created_at. Read ORDER BY created_at, id.
- ONE trigger, trg_med_order_events_no_update. Deliberately NO no-delete trigger: (i) a DELETE-abort table must either be retained after a patient erasure, which keeps drug names, doses and reasons (PHI) beyond the erasure and is a decision for Samuel (MO-R13), or it breaks test_erase_plan_retained; (ii) the reseed keeps DELETE-abort tables, so every morning's reseed would leave orphan events on reseeded patient ids, polluting timelines and the X013 counts; (iii) precedent: medication_administrations is append-only by design with no trigger. Tamper evidence comes from the hash-chained clinical_access audit row written beside every event.
- Both tables are added to consent_service._RETENTION_SOURCES under 'prescription_and_dispensing' (created_at). Erase plan and reseed pick them up from their patient_id column with no edit.

Column additions:
- medications ADD COLUMN med_order_id TEXT (UNIQUE partial index), held_at TEXT, hold_reason TEXT. held_at is the projection marker every administration-driving reader checks (section 7); it is NULL on every legacy row.
- helix_patient_med_orders ADD COLUMN med_order_id TEXT: in the migration (guarded on the table existing, the m35 pattern) AND in HELIX_SCHEMA's CREATE TABLE (fresh databases create Helix tables after the runner). Its index is created only by the migration and by a column-guarded step in init_helix_db, never inside the HELIX_SCHEMA executescript, because 22 test files call init_helix_db and on a legacy table without the column an unguarded CREATE INDEX aborts the rest of the script.
- No change to orders, medication_administrations or the override tables.

ADOPTION (not in the migration; migrations stay schema-only)
- medorder_service.adopt_legacy() runs at boot when ORB_MED_ORDER_STORE is on, from server/scripts/medorder_parity.py --adopt, and from POST /api/medorders/admin/adopt. Idempotent, 500 rows per transaction, guarded by the unique index. NEVER on a GET path (the main.py:324-340 rule: SQLite is single-writer).
- Pure mapping legacy_status_for(row), also used by GET routes to show unlinked rows as legacy items without writing:
  - active or prn -> prescribed, or verified when verified_by is set; projection_status = old status.
  - needs_verification = 1 for llm_extracted and agentic.
  - discontinued + AI source + verified_by set -> rejected (reject_medication is the only writer of that combination, pharmacy_verification_service.py:417).
  - any other discontinued -> stopped, reason 'stopped before the order store', projection_status NULL.
- Unlinked Helix rows are not adopted (a Sage pair cannot be matched reliably); the parity report lists them.
- Adopting unverified AI rows before medorders-5a is safe under I1: the eMAR still reads verified_by from the projection, and the legacy verify mirror (medorders-3) moves the store.

2. LIFECYCLE
LEGAL_TRANSITIONS:
- draft -> prescribed | cancelled
- prescribed -> verified | rejected | held | stopped | cancelled (cancelled only before any given dose)
- verified -> held | stopped | completed
- held -> held_from (prescribed or verified) | stopped
- stopped, completed, cancelled, rejected are terminal.
Dispensed and administered are EVENTS, not statuses (a TDS course is dispensed many times and given 15 times).

order_allows_dose(order): consulted by the eMAR for LINKED rows, for 'given' only, IN ADDITION to the unchanged legacy checks on the projection row:
- prescribed or verified: allowed (the legacy check still demands verified_by for AI sources, I1);
- held: refused, naming who held it, when and why, and saying 'not given (held)' can always be recorded;
- draft or terminal: refused (unreachable in practice: drafts have no projection, terminal orders project 'discontinued').
MO-R1 (follow-on) later adds: projection.verified_by required for every linked order, with the ruled stat exception.

Projection rules (project_in_txn):
- draft: no medications row.
- prescribed, verified: status = projection_status, held_at NULL.
- held: status UNCHANGED (the interaction screen and the regimen still see it), held_at and hold_reason set.
- stopped, completed, cancelled, rejected: 'discontinued', held_at NULL.
- verified_by/verified_at are copied to the projection on verify (I1).
- CPOE mirror: the store writes orders.status itself, as a guarded UPDATE orders SET status=? WHERE id=? AND status=? plus an order_events row, inside the store transaction; never through orders_service.transition_order (it has no active->completed edge). Map: draft->draft; prescribed, verified, held->active; stopped, cancelled, rejected->cancelled; completed->completed. All fit the orders CHECK (database.py:812).
- FHIR MedicationRequest.status: draft, active, on-hold, stopped, completed, cancelled (rejected maps to cancelled with a statusReason).

3. SERVICE: server/services/medorder_service.py
- Pure: LEGAL_TRANSITIONS, order_allows_dose(), legacy_status_for(), projection_for(), fhir_status_for(), screen_fingerprint().
- In-transaction cores (take a connection, never commit, never open a session): create_in_txn, transition_in_txn (UPDATE ... WHERE id=? AND version=? AND status=?; rowcount 0 raises StaleOrderVersion), project_in_txn, record_event_in_txn, request_supply_in_txn (idempotent per order: returns the existing non-terminal linked supply row, else helix_service.insert_order(conn, ...) at 'pending' with the exact formulary_id; insert_order needs no change), mirror_legacy_decision_in_txn (legacy verify/reject hook), on_supply_transition_in_txn (the Helix callback), adopt_medication_in_txn.
- Public steps: create, sign, verify, reject, hold, resume, stop, cancel, amend_placeholders, request_supply. Each runs:
  (1) Load the order.
  (2) Run the gate OUTSIDE any write transaction: enforce_medication_safety with the order's own drug, dose, route, the actor's role, entry_point 'medorder.<step>.<lane>' and exclude_med_id = the projection id (new keyword passthrough, default None, medorders-1). Why outside: db_session(immediate=True) must be the outermost session (database.py:1150-1162); on the unpooled path the gate's own sessions would contend with our write lock for the full busy timeout; and the gate's denial audit rows must not roll back with a refused step.
  (3) db_session(immediate=True): re-read; check expected_version and screen_fingerprint (hash of active allergy ids and states plus the live order and unlinked active row ids). Mismatch answers 409 screen_stale so the client re-screens (closes W116c).
  (4) Status, event, projection, CPOE mirror, supply row and clinical_access audit in that one transaction.
  (5) Return the order and the safety verdict.
- Gate points: create-as-prescribed and sign: full screen with dose; verify: full screen with dose and the pharmacist's role (a dose block still goes back to the prescriber), excluding the projection, and when a product is bound its name is screened too; resume: full screen, excluding the projection; Helix steps on a linked row: the effective drug as today plus exclusion, dose and role.
- Formulary binding at verify is allowed only when the product's ingredient set equals the order's (helix_medication_master.generic_name resolved through drug_safety_service.interaction_terms ingredient terms). Any other product is a substitution: refused with 'this is a substitution and needs the prescriber' until R002 is ruled (medorders-15).
- Errors: StaleOrderVersion and StaleScreen 409 with the current order; TransitionNotAllowed 409; NeedsInput 422; NotPermitted 403.
- Queries: list_for_patient (read-only: linked orders plus unlinked rows shown via legacy_status_for); get; events; verification_queue(dept) and to_sign_queue(dept) filtered with permissions.scope_patient_ids_sql(dept); nurse_entered_live(dept); parity_report().

4. LANE ADAPTERS
Store flag (record mode): chart, Sage handoff, Scribe. Lifecycle flag: CPOE, order sets, sign, unified verification, hold, resume, stop, cancel, store-backed screening. The CPOE adapters are LIFECYCLE ONLY (in record mode a draft order reaches nothing anyway).
- Chart add (vigil.med_add), both modes: the route calls await run_db(medorder_service.create_chart_order, ...), which runs the same gate call and then one transaction: the idempotency pre-check and medications INSERT exactly as _insert_medication, the med_order (prescribed, prescriber = actor, entered_by_role recorded), event and audit. This also takes the gate off the event loop (F-D). Add status 'prn' sets is_prn; 'discontinued' at add creates a stopped order.
  Under lifecycle the chart lane does NOT change: a nurse still charts a live order and can still acknowledge a severe-allergy alert there (medication_safety_gate.py:250). That is R010/R011 territory and stays. So Sign makes a prescriber's signature the release step for CPOE and order-set drugs ONLY; the chart lane bypasses Sign until R010 is ruled. Nurse-entered live orders are listed in the prescriber's to-sign view under 'Entered by a nurse' for visibility, without gating.
- CPOE and order sets (lifecycle): each medication order or item also creates a draft med_order linked by cpoe_order_id or order_set_application_id. Sign needs medication.prescribe. /orders/{id}/transition on a LINKED order (keyed on the link, so it holds after the flag goes off): to_status 'cancelled' delegates to medorder_service.cancel with section 8's permissions; every other target answers 409 managed_by_medication_order with the med_order_id. Shadow: under lifecycle a medication CPOE order or order-set medication item emits clinical.action at SIGN only (actor = signer); create stops emitting for medication. Lifecycle off: unchanged.
- Sage handoff (store flag): one transaction holds the chart row (llm_extracted, as today), the med_order (prescribed, prescriber = confirming actor as today, needs_verification 1) and the linked supply row. The product is bound by the SAME LIKE lookup create_order uses today, run on the same connection through helix_service.resolve_by_name_in_txn(conn, name), extracted from create_order (:243-250) with no behaviour change. 'charted-only' is kept when nothing matches. Exact binding through the reconciler is a separate behaviour change (medorders-20), because rxnorm_reconciler is fuzzy (0.8 threshold, substring boosted to 0.85) and the gate screens the free-text target. The synchronous call at relay_routes.py:420 is NOT moved by this epic (sage_handoff_service.py:505-521 landmine); see risks.
- Scribe extraction (store flag): one med_order per start inside _persist_extraction's transaction; prescriber = note author, needs_verification 1, no supply row, [SAFETY] note kept. Drafts instead are W111 (medorders-13).
- Helix approve and Relay confirm_agentic: legacy until R010 and W099.
- History import and scripts: unlinked; adopted at the next boot or by the adopt action.

5. PHARMACIST VERIFICATION
- Record mode: the Verify Queue keeps calling pharmacy_verification_service. On a LINKED row, its UPDATE is followed in the same session by mirror_legacy_decision_in_txn (a 'verified' or 'rejected' event and status; a held order records held_from='verified'). Helix transitions and receipt on a linked supply row write supply_reviewing, supply_verified, dispensed and received events only; they do not change the order's status.
- Lifecycle: verify() and reject() are the one decision.
  - Verify Queue routes call medorder_service for linked rows; pharmacy_verification_service stays the path for unlinked rows.
  - Helix route, linked row: helix_routes runs the gate (effective drug, exclusion, dose, role), then calls helix_service.transition_order_status(..., on_applied=callback). The callback runs inside Helix's own session just before its commit and calls transition_in_txn for verified or rejected; a lost version race raises and rolls back the Helix transition too. The public verify() is never called from inside helix_service (immediate must be outermost). receive_order gains the same optional callback.
  - Whichever surface verifies first verifies the ORDER (status verified; projection verified_by and verified_at). The Verify Queue then stops listing it; the Helix modal shows 'Order verified by X at T', and the Helix verified step is a supply step that does not re-verify the order.
  - Placeholders: for linked rows, verify refuses 'REVIEW REQUIRED' on either surface (reusing _is_placeholder); corrections are 'amended' events with before and after values, allowed only on needs_verification orders (the F012 ruling applied once). This closes F-A for linked rows.
- Supply: NO automatic supply row for chart or CPOE orders until MO-R12 is ruled. Lanes that create one today keep doing so (Sage handoff). A 'Request from pharmacy' action on a live, formulary-bound order calls request_supply_in_txn, which is idempotent (one open supply row per order). Verification never creates a supply row, so a Sage order has exactly one. Supply rows always start 'pending' through the unchanged insert_order, and the case-room message still comes from Helix's own transition path.
- Custody, scoped down: an 'administered' event carries a supply id only when exactly one linked supply row is 'delivered' with received_by set and no earlier administered event references it (Helix dispenses one unit per row). Otherwise the event records 'supply not linked'. Lot-to-dose custody for multi-unit supply and ward stock moves to the pharmacy GRN epic.

6. eMAR: record_administration (emar_service.py:489), linked rows only
- The order-state check applies to 'given' only and sits BELOW the idempotent replay check (:577) and the discharged-patient guard (:582-604), for the reason the file gives: a replay must never get a 4xx that the offline client treats as a failed sync.
- Pre-check before the allergy interlock, for a clean refusal before the nurse is prompted.
- Re-check AFTER the medication_administrations INSERT, inside the same transaction: the INSERT holds the write lock, so no hold can commit in between; a held order raises and the dose rolls back. db_session(immediate=True) for the whole call was rejected because it serialises every dose on the ward.
- 'not_given' is always allowed, including 'not given (held)' on a held order (the file's own principle: withholding must always be easy).
- The 'administered' or 'not_given' event commits with the MAR row and its audit, or not at all.
- Unlinked rows untouched; PRN unchanged until MO-R3.

7. HELD STATE IN EVERY READER
Readers of medications today, and what held does to each:
- Administration-driving (medorders-6a): emar_service (link check, section 6); nurse_shift_service.py:325-330 (held rows go to an on_hold list, no due or overdue); downtime_service.py:162-166 (a separate 'ON HOLD: do not give' section on the paper MAR, because paper has no link check); MedRoundSheet (On hold group, no Administer); voice_agent_service.py:132 (labelled, never read out as due).
- Presentation (medorders-6b): ipass_service.py:315 ('on hold since T: reason'); discharge_service.py:270 ('on hold'); bridge_routes.py:243 and :354 (plain text 'On hold', no colour and no explanation, in line with the portal rules); fhir_export_service.py:341 (on-hold); sage_service.py:3071 and sage_ambient_service.py:1315 (labelled); scribe_service.py:79 and patient_specific_screen.py:371 (kept in the set, held drugs still interact); vigil_routes.py:101 (SELECT * carries held_at to the UI).
- Counts, unchanged and stated: forecast_service, impact_service, coding_service, sage_proactive_service.
- test_medorder_reader_registry.py lists every module that reads FROM medications and fails on any module missing from this table, so a new reader cannot silently treat a held drug as givable.

product_rulings.question: MO-R1: Must every medication order be verified by a pharmacist before its first dose? Today only AI or agentic sources need it.
product_rulings.options: (a) Every order; stat and urgent first doses may be given at 'prescribed' and verified afterwards, flagged on the MAR. (b) AI or agentic only, as today. (c) Every order, no exceptions.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a), with a retrospective window set by the site pharmacist (suggest before the next scheduled dose). Follow-on medorders-11.

product_rulings.question: MO-R2: Who may hold, resume, stop, and cancel a live medication order? Today no route does any of these.
product_rulings.options: (a) The prescriber (medication.prescribe) for all four; the nurse records a single dose as not given, as today; the pharmacist rejects or queries in Relay. (b) As (a), and nurses may also hold for nil-by-mouth or a procedure, with the prescriber told. (c) Pharmacists may also hold pending a query.

issues.issue: Linked rows go stale when a legacy UPDATE writer changes them, and the eMAR then refuses doses that are verified. The strangler assumes legacy writers only produce UNLINKED rows, but some legacy writers UPDATE rows that are already linked. medorders-2 adopts llm_extracted rows as prescribed with needs_verification=1. medorders-3 then ships the link-keyed administrable() check. The Verify Queue is only converted in medorders-5 (5 depends on 4, which depends on 3). The same thing happens permanently on any database that ran with the store on and then turned it off: the links persist, the eMAR check ignores flags, and the legacy verify never writes the store. first_draft.design:
PRINCIPLE
- One authoritative record, med_orders, plus an append-only ledger, med_order_events.
- The four existing tables stay. Each is demoted to one role:
  - medications becomes the order's WARD PROJECTION. About 25 readers already read it: nurse board, eMAR, I-PASS, Sage, Bridge, FHIR, downtime pack, discharge, timeline and others.
  - helix_patient_med_orders becomes the order's SUPPLY child: one row per dispense request, many per order.
  - orders (type medication) becomes the CPOE VIEW of a draft.
  - medication_administrations stays the MAR child, keyed by the projection row.
- Nothing is renamed, rebuilt or dropped.
- Strangler: medorder_service becomes the writer of all four tables through per-lane adapters. Rows written behind its back (tests, seeds, history import, unconverted lanes) stay valid as UNLINKED legacy rows with exactly today's semantics, and are adopted when read.

1. DATA MODEL
One additive migration, numbered with the next free number after 47 at merge time (never pre-assigned). The five sibling HIS epics and about ten sessions share migrations.py.

med_orders: no declared FOREIGN KEYs, following the m20 rule 1 at migrations.py:1771. This means med_orders is never an FK parent, so a future status CHECK widening is an ordinary in-transaction rebuild (the m39 shape), not the users trap.
- id TEXT PRIMARY KEY (uuid4)
- patient_id TEXT NOT NULL
- admission_id TEXT: the active admission when the order is created
- encounter_type TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'ip', CHECK in ('ip','op','discharge'). Reserved now so the OPD epic does not force a rebuild.
- status TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK in ('draft','prescribed','verified','held','stopped','completed','cancelled','rejected')
- version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1: optimistic concurrency, like sage_actions.version
- source TEXT NOT NULL: chart | cpoe | order_set | sage_handoff | relay_agentic | helix_approve | scribe_extracted | history_import | legacy_adopted | verbal
- needs_verification INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0: 1 for today's _UNVERIFIED_SOURCES
- drug_name TEXT NOT NULL
- formulary_id TEXT: helix_medication_master.id, bound by exact id and never by LIKE
- dose, route, frequency TEXT
- schedule_kind TEXT: the nurse_shift_service.parse_frequency kind, stored at write time
- is_prn INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, and prn_indication TEXT
- priority TEXT, CHECK in ('routine','urgent','stat')
- start_at, end_at, duration_text TEXT: lets discharge print a real course instead of a 5-day default
- indication, notes TEXT
- entered_by TEXT NOT NULL, entered_by_role TEXT
- prescriber_id, prescribed_at
- verified_by, verified_at
- status_reason, status_changed_by, status_changed_at
- last_safety_json, last_screened_at, screen_fingerprint
- projection_status TEXT: 'active' or 'prn', the legacy status the projection carries while the order is live
- legacy_medication_id INTEGER
- cpoe_order_id TEXT, order_set_application_id INTEGER
- sage_action_id, sage_handoff_id, scribe_note_id TEXT
- idempotency_key TEXT
- facility_id TEXT: NULL means the single site; the multi-site epic fills it
- created_at, updated_at TEXT, written with services.clinical_time.utc_iso_now()
Indexes:
- (patient_id, status)
- (status, needs_verification)
- (cpoe_order_id)
- (admission_id)
- UNIQUE(legacy_medication_id) WHERE NOT NULL
- UNIQUE(idempotency_key) WHERE NOT NULL

med_order_events (append-only):
- id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT
- med_order_id TEXT NOT NULL
- patient_id TEXT NOT NULL
- kind: created | signed | verified | rejected | held | resumed | stopped | completed | cancelled | amended | adopted | supply_requested | dispensed | received | administered | not_given | countersigned
- from_status, to_status
- actor_id, actor_role
- entry_point: for example 'vigil.med_add', 'orders.cpoe', 'helix.verified'
- reason
- ref_type, ref_id: an administration id, Helix transition id or stock movement id
- payload_json: before and after values for amendments, and the safety verdict
- idempotency_key, with a UNIQUE partial index
- created_at
Triggers trg_med_order_events_no_update and trg_med_order_events_no_delete, the m14 consent pattern. Reads are ordered ORDER BY created_at, id.

Column additions:
- medications ADD COLUMN med_order_id TEXT, with a UNIQUE partial index.
- helix_patient_med_orders ADD COLUMN med_order_id TEXT, with an index. Guarded on the table existing (the m35 pattern), AND added to HELIX_SCHEMA in helix_db.py. Fresh databases create Helix tables after the runner, so without the second site they would never get the column.
- No change to orders, medication_administrations or the override tables.

Adoption is NOT in the migration. Migrations stay schema-only and safe to ledger. medorder_service.adopt_legacy() runs at boot only when ORB_MED_ORDER_STORE is on. It is idempotent, chunked at 500 rows per transaction, and guarded by the unique index. Mapping:
- active or prn becomes prescribed, or verified when verified_by is set.
- needs_verification is set for llm_extracted and agentic rows.
- discontinued becomes stopped, with the reason 'stopped before the order store'.
- projection_status is the old status.
- Helix rows without a link are NOT adopted. A Sage pair cannot be matched reliably to its chart row, so those rows stay on the legacy flow and appear in the parity report.

2. LIFECYCLE
LEGAL_TRANSITIONS:
- draft -> prescribed | cancelled
- prescribed -> verified | rejected | held | stopped | cancelled (cancelled only before any dose)
- verified -> held | stopped | completed
- held -> prescribed or verified (resume, back to the state it was held from) | stopped
- stopped, completed, cancelled and rejected are terminal.

The brief's 'dispensed' and 'administered' are EVENTS on the order, not its status. A TDS course for 5 days is dispensed several times and given 15 times, and Helix's one-unit dispense model needs many supply rows per order. The timeline UI still shows all eight milestones.

administrable(order) is the one function the eMAR consults:
- verified, or
- prescribed with needs_verification = 0 (today's rule for orders a person entered, until MO-R1 is ruled);
- never draft, held or terminal.
Projected PRN-status rows stay refused until MO-R3 is ruled.

Projection rules (project_in_txn):
- draft: no medications row, so drafts never leak to legacy readers.
- prescribed, verified and held: one row whose status is projection_status, so held drugs stay in every reader's regimen and the interaction screen. The eMAR refuses them through the order link.
- stopped, completed, cancelled and rejected: the row becomes 'discontinued'.
- orders.status for a CPOE-linked order is mirrored: draft->draft; prescribed, verified and held->active; stopped, cancelled and rejected->cancelled; completed->completed. Every value fits the existing CHECK.
- FHIR MedicationRequest.status: draft, active, on-hold, stopped, completed, cancelled.

3. SERVICE: server/services/medorder_service.py
- Pure helpers: LEGAL_TRANSITIONS, ADMINISTRABLE, administrable(), projection_status_for(), fhir_status_for().
- In-transaction cores take a connection, never commit and never open a second connection: create_in_txn, transition_in_txn, project_in_txn, record_event_in_txn, request_supply_in_txn (helix_service.insert_order(conn, ...) by exact formulary_id) and adopt_medication_in_txn. These let Relay's single-transaction confirm (R024) and Scribe's _persist_extraction join their callers' transactions.
- Public steps: create, sign, verify, reject, hold, resume, stop, cancel, amend_placeholders.
- Each public step runs in this order:
  (1) Load the order.
  (2) Run the gate OUTSIDE any write transaction: enforce_medication_safety with the order's OWN drug, dose and route plus the actor's role, entry_point 'medorder.<step>.<lane>'. The gate opens its own connections and audit writes, and running it inside a write transaction is the WAL self-deadlock.
  (3) Open db_session(immediate=True). Re-read the order, then check expected_version and screen_fingerprint (a hash of the active allergy row ids and states plus the live order ids). On mismatch, answer 409 screen_stale, so the client re-screens. This closes the screen-to-write window (W116c).
  (4) Write the status, the event, the projection, any supply row and the audit in that one transaction, then commit.
  (5) Return the order and the safety verdict.
- Gate points:
  - create-as-prescribed and sign: full screen including the dose;
  - verify: full screen, excluding the order's own projection row; a dose block stays prescriber-only, as today;
  - resume: full screen;
  - Helix dispensed: effective drug, as today.
  The bedside interlock and dose guard stay in emar_service, unchanged, as the last line at the moment of the dose.
- Errors: StaleOrderVersion and StaleScreen give 409 with the current order; TransitionNotAllowed gives 409; NeedsInput gives 422; NotPermitted gives 403.
- Queries:
  - list_for_patient: lazily adopts unlinked rows;
  - get and events;
  - verification_queue(dept) and to_sign_queue(dept): same admissions.department join as helix_service.orders_awaiting_receipt (:536), department from permissions.department_scope;
  - parity_report().

4. LANE ADAPTERS
All behind ORB_MED_ORDER_STORE. Each preserves today's behaviour; anything that changes behaviour is its own increment.
- Chart add (vigil.med_add): status prescribed, prescriber is the actor (as today), projection is the same row as today. One transaction replaces get_db().commit().
- CPOE and order sets: a draft linked by cpoe_order_id or order_set_application_id. Signing needs medication.prescribe. A nurse can still create drafts (R010 untouched); only a prescriber's signature makes one reach the ward.
- Sage handoff: prescribed, prescriber is the confirming actor (as today), needs_verification = 1. The chart row and the linked supply row are written in ONE transaction, using the reconciled id instead of LIKE.
- Scribe extraction: prescribed, prescriber is the note author (as today), needs_verification = 1, no supply row. Turning these into drafts is W111.
- Helix approve and Relay confirm_agentic: left on the legacy flow until R010 and W099 are ruled.
- History import and seeds: unlinked, adopted when read.

5. PHARMACIST VERIFICATION IN ONE PLACE
- verify() and reject() are called both by the Verify Queue routes (pharmacy_routes.py:53, :116) and by Helix reviewing->verified/rejected on a linked row (helix_service.transition_order_status).
- Record mode mirrors each of today's two verifications separately. Lifecycle mode makes one decision move both rows.
- Placeholder correction is allowed only on needs_verification orders, reusing _is_placeholder, so the F012 ruling applies once. Each correction is an 'amended' event with before and after values.
- Verification binds the exact formulary product and creates the supply row at Helix status 'verified', with a helix_transitions row whose payload notes the med order. Scheduling, dispensing and ward receipt then run unchanged.
- dispensed and received on linked rows write order events.
- An 'administered' event carries the latest received supply id. That is the custody link from lot to dispense to receipt to dose.

6. eMAR
record_administration gains a check for rows with med_order_id: it refuses unless administrable(), with text naming the order state and who to call. It also writes 'administered' or 'not_given' in the same transaction as the MAR row and its audit. The check keys on the LINK, not the flag, so switching the lifecycle flag off can never make a held order givable. Unlinked rows are untouched.

7. ROUTES: server/routes/medorder_routes.py, prefix /api/medorders
- All handlers are def (run on the threadpool).
- Every route answers 404 when the store flag is off (the billing_routes.py:84 pattern). Write routes answer 404 unless the lifecycle flag is on.
- Routes:
  - GET /patient/{patient_id}: require_patient_access(patient.read_all, audit_action='med_orders_viewed')
  - GET /{id} and GET /{id}/events: _in_scope_or_404 plus log_phi_read
  - POST '' (create): enforce_patient_scope, Idempotency-Key
  - POST /{id}/sign: medication.prescribe, safety_ack, expected_version
  - POST /{id}/verify and /{id}/reject: medication.verify
  - POST /{id}/hold, /{id}/resume and /{id}/stop: medication.prescribe, pending MO-R2
  - POST /{id}/cancel
  - GET /queue/verification and GET /queue/to-sign
  - GET /admin/parity: admin.overview
- Out-of-ward access answers 404, never 403, with a patient_scope_denied audit row.
- After commit, the route emits 'medorders:update' {patient_id, med_order_id, status} to the patient room via sio, as relay_routes does. ws/realtime.py is not edited.

8. PERMISSIONS
- No new role: roles.STORABLE_ROLES is unchanged.
- One new constant in permissions.py, MEDICATION_VERIFY = 'medication.verify'. It goes to the pharmacist, and to admin only to preserve today's helix.write reach until MO-R4 (W178) is ruled. Mirrored in src/lib/roles.ts and covered by the test_rbac parity test.

- Draft creation reuses ORDER_WRITE or MEDICATION_WRITE.
- The pharmacist stays hospital-wide (F109).

9. AUDIT
- Every state change writes log_audit_event: event_category 'clinical_access' (fail-closed), on db=conn in the same transaction. action_type is med_order_<verb>, target_type 'med_order', target_id str(id) (string ids avoid the int target_id false-tamper trap), with the patient_id. metadata carries from, to, entry_point, lane, reason and the safety summary.
- The gate keeps its own clinical_safety rows (fail-open by design).
- Reads use log_phi_read (phi_access, fail-closed).
- Adoption writes one 'med_orders_adopted' row per batch, with counts.

- A new default-off helper, _feature_on(env), that accepts only explicit 1/true/on/yes. The existing _module_enabled defaults ON and must not be reused. The first HIS epic to land adds the helper; the others reuse it.

product_rulings.question: MO-R1: Must every medication order be verified by a pharmacist before its first dose? Which orders are exempt? Today only AI or agentic-sourced drugs need verification.
product_rulings.options: (a) Every order. Stat and urgent first doses may be given at 'prescribed' and verified afterwards, flagged on the MAR. (b) Only AI or agentic sources, as today. (c) Every order, no exceptions.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). The retrospective window is set by the site pharmacist; suggest before the next scheduled dose.

product_rulings.question: MO-R2: Who may put a medication order on hold, resume it, and stop it? Today no route does any of these.
product_rulings.options: (a) The prescriber (medication.prescribe) for all three. The nurse records a single dose as not given, as she can today. The pharmacist rejects an order or raises a query in Relay. (b) As (a), and nurses may also hold for nil-by-mouth or a procedure, with the prescriber told. (c) Pharmacists may also hold pending a query.

product_rulings.question: MO-R3: Should a drug charted with status PRN be givable? Today it shows on the round but every dose is refused (emar_service.py:556). And should the order-time interaction and duplicate screen include PRN, held and signed CPOE orders, but not unsigned drafts?
product_rulings.options: (a) Yes to both. (b) Givable, but keep screening on 'active' only. (c) Leave as today.

product_rulings.question: MO-R4 (W178): Should an administrator keep the ability to verify medication orders? Today they can, through helix.write.
product_rulings.options: (a) Pharmacist only; a site may grant it to others. (b) Keep admin.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). In code it stays granted to admin until you rule, so nothing changes silently.

product_rulings.question: MO-R5: Should acknowledging a SEVERE allergy alert at order time need medication.prescribe on every lane, as the bedside override has since 2026-08-15? Today anyone with medication.write or order.write can type a reason (medication_safety_gate.py:250).
product_rulings.options: (a) Prescriber-only on every lane. (b) Prescriber-only on the new sign step only. (c) As today.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). The store's sign step is prescriber-only by construction. The nurse chart-lane part overlaps R010 and R011, which are held, so that lane waits.

product_rulings.question: MO-R6: At order time the same ingredient is already on a live order. Should Orb show a notice, require a 428 acknowledgement with a reason, or block?
product_rulings.options: (a) Notice only. (b) 428 with a reason, recorded. (c) Hard block.
product_rulings.recommendation: (b). Stat top-ups and route changes are legitimate, so never a hard block.

product_rulings.question: MO-R7: What happens to live medication orders at discharge, death or transfer?
product_rulings.options: (a) Complete them with the reason 'discharged' only after the discharge reconciliation is signed; transfer keeps them live and prompts a transfer reconciliation. (b) Complete them automatically at discharge. (c) Leave them live, as today.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). Never close an order silently. The discharge gate itself is R009, which stays held.

product_rulings.question: MO-R8 (W117): What are the standard administration times for each frequency, for example TDS as 08/14/20 or 06/14/22?
product_rulings.options: (a) A site_config file signed by pharmacy and the physician champion. (b) Built-in defaults. (c) Keep the derived schedule.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a), with no built-in default. Until a site signs one, the derived schedule continues.

product_rulings.question: MO-R9: If the lifecycle flag is switched off after use, held orders stay ungivable, because the bedside check follows the order link rather than the flag. They then have to be re-prescribed from the chart. Accept?
product_rulings.options: (a) Accept: it fails closed. (b) Release held orders when the flag goes off.

product_rulings.question: MO-R10: What happens to drafts nobody signs, for example order-set drafts?
product_rulings.options: (a) Never auto-cancel. Show drafts older than 24 h at the top of the to-sign queue and on handover. (b) Auto-cancel after a site-set time, with a Relay note.

product_rulings.question: MO-R11: May a CPOE medication order name a drug that is not on the formulary?
product_rulings.options: (a) Allow free text with a visible line saying it is not supplied by pharmacy; the pharmacist binds a product at verification. (b) Formulary products only.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a) until the drug-master work in the GRN epic lands, then revisit.

risks: Dual writes can diverge during the move. Any path that writes the legacy tables outside medorder_service creates unlinked rows: 37 test files, the seed and reset scripts, history import and populate_helix_from_medgemma.py. Mitigation: unlinked rows keep today's semantics, are adopted when read, the parity report counts them, and the AST guard closes the door at the end.

Adoption decides who can be given a dose, because the bedside check follows the order link. A wrong status mapping would refuse or allow real doses. Run the table-driven equivalence test (status x source x verified_by) before any site turns the store on.

WAL self-deadlock and blocking the event loop. enforce_medication_safety opens its own connections and writes audit rows, so calling it inside an open write transaction deadlocks. Screen outside the transaction and re-check the fingerprint inside. Every new handler is a def handler or uses run_db. The Relay transition already calls create_and_dispatch_handoff synchronously on the loop (relay_routes.py:420), and medorders-8 adds work to that call.
FK-parent rebuild trap. medications is the FK parent of three tables and must never be rebuilt. The new tables declare no FKs, so they are never FK parents.
Helix tables are created outside the migration runner. If the HELIX_SCHEMA twin of med_order_id is forgotten, fresh databases silently lack the column (the m35 lesson).

A green suite on a fresh database hides failures on legacy databases (orb-verification-lessons). Every migration and adoption test needs a tmp_path legacy database, and the suite must not be run with the shipping .env.
Audit int target_id false-tamper alarm. Always pass str(id). Legacy medication ids are integers.
The shadow scorecard can double-count. CPOE create already emits clinical.action (orders_routes.py:315), so a signature must not emit a second event for the same decision.
Switching the lifecycle flag off after use leaves held orders ungivable and removes the resume route. It fails closed, but needs MO-R9 and an operations note.

Size. The coverage map estimates 2 to 4 weeks plus a week of gating. The honest total is about 65 engineer-days, of which about 30 can start now. The difference is eight lanes instead of the three the map counted, the dual-run and parity work, the UI, and increments held for rulings.

Formulary quality. Without the drug-master work (GRN epic), most orders have no exact product and get no supply row, so the pharmacy keeps working the legacy way for them. The seed tags two brands with the wrong generic, which would bind the wrong product at verification.

Duplicate prescribing during the move. With lifecycle on, a doctor can sign a CPOE or order-set draft for a drug they already charted from the chart, which the MED_NOT_SENT copy told them to do. Until MO-R6 is ruled, the sign screen shows only a notice.

Hot shared files across about ten sessions and five sibling epics: config.py, migrations.py, permissions.py, main.py and shellConfig.tsx. Take migration numbers at merge time and land each increment as its own commit now that git exists.
Ward Record and the demos depend on both flags staying off. A demo that turns the store on gets its reseeded legacy rows adopted at boot automatically; check the parity report before presenting.
